newsitem.title: ITALY: Benetton may float Sportsystem in N.Y., profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Benetton may float Sportsystem in N.Y., profits rise.

text.p: Italian clothing company Benetton said Monday it may float its entire Sportsystem division on the New York stock market by the end of 1997, including the Rollerblade skates and Prince tennis brand.
Sportsystem is held by the Benetton family group Edizione Holdings, which itself holds a majority stake in Benetton.

A Benetton spokeswoman said the idea was to quote the division in New York where the main brands were based. "It will certainly be New York. Analysis is going on but no date has been fixed yet, it could be by the end of 1997," she said.
Commenting on a press report about a possible listing in London next summer, the spokeswoman said it was premature to talk of a London stock offering.
Benetton had originally planned a Wall Street listing of Rollerblade this summer.
Separately, Benetton reported a 9 percent increase in first-half profits and forecast a similar gain during the second half.
The company, based in Ponzano in northeastern Italy and with franchised stores in 120 countries, said group consolidated first-half net profits rose to 115.8 billion lire ($76 million).
Earlier this month, Group Chairman Luciano Benetton said first-half revenue would be flat and net profits show only a slight increase with trading conditions remaining difficult.

Managing Director Carlo Gilardi said Benetton raised its prices a little less than average inflation levels, and while labour costs had also gone up, the group had not suffered significantly from fluctuations in raw material prices like wool and cotton.

Benetton's costs in the first half suffered from the high value of the lira with 80 percent of its produce manufactured in Italy, but this was largely offset by profits from its foreign exchange activities.
First half sales were marginally higher at 1.47 trillion lire ($966 million).
